name: Grattan Bridge
facts: Grattan Bridge, originally Essex Bridge, opened in 1676 and was rebuilt in 1753 by George Semple, featuring stone alcoves and niches inspired by London Bridge's design.
In 1874, the bridge was widened and flattened by Parke Neville, adopting Westminster Bridge's style and adding ornate cast‑iron lamp standards that still illuminate the Liffey today.
The 2002 reconstruction replaced the deck with granite paving and benches, while 2004 temporary kiosks—intended to emulate Florence's Ponte Vecchio—were later removed amid controversy.
